rice.why_grown: Rice is India's staple food grain, widely cultivated for high yield potential and strong domestic demand.
rice.common_uses: Staple food grain, puffed rice, rice flour, and cattle feed from straw.
rice.season: Kharif (Monsoon) in most states; Rabi/Summer in coastal and irrigated areas.
rice.soil: Clay loam or heavy clay soils with good water retention capacity.
rice.climate: Warm, humid climate with temperatures between 20°C–37°C and high moisture.
rice.key_characteristics: High water requirement; responds well to organic and nitrogenous fertilizers.

paddy.why_grown: Paddy (unhusked rice) is the primary Kharif cereal crop supporting smallholder farm incomes across India.
paddy.common_uses: Milling into rice, bran oil extraction, and agricultural fodder.
paddy.season: Kharif (June–November) and Rabi in southern/eastern belts.
paddy.soil: Alluvial and clay loam soils capable of holding standing water.
paddy.climate: Tropical and subtropical climate with adequate seasonal rainfall.
paddy.key_characteristics: Requires flooded conditions or regular irrigation during flowering stage.

wheat.why_grown: Wheat is the premier Rabi cereal crop, essential for food security and cereal economics in North and Central India.
wheat.common_uses: Atta (flour), suji, maida, bread, biscuits, and traditional flatbreads (chapatis).
wheat.soil: Well-drained fertile loamy soils and clay loams.
wheat.climate: Cool winters during vegetative growth and warm dry conditions for harvesting (15°C–25°C).
wheat.key_characteristics: Moderate water requirement; sensitive to excessive rainfall at harvest.

maize.why_grown: Maize (Corn) is a versatile cereal grown for food, feed, and industrial starch production.
maize.common_uses: Poultry feed, cattle feed, human food, corn starch, and ethanol production.
maize.soil: Deep, well-drained loamy soils rich in organic matter.
maize.key_characteristics: Drought tolerant; susceptible to waterlogging in early stages.

potato.why_grown: Potato is a high-yielding horticultural cash crop providing high economic returns per hectare.
potato.common_uses: Fresh vegetable consumption, chips, processing, and food manufacturing.
potato.season: Rabi (October–February) in plains; Kharif in hill regions.
potato.soil: Loose, well-drained sandy loam soil rich in humus.
potato.climate: Cool climate with night temperatures around 15°C–20°C for optimal tuberization.
potato.key_characteristics: Short duration crop (90–110 days); requires frequent light irrigation.

onion.why_grown: Onion is an essential vegetable crop with steady market demand and significant commercial value.
onion.common_uses: Culinary spice/vegetable in daily diets, processing, and export.
onion.soil: Friable, well-drained sandy loam or silt loam soils.
onion.climate: Mild, cool climate without extreme heat or severe frost.
onion.key_characteristics: Shallow rooted; sensitive to soil moisture stress and high weed competition.

soybean.why_grown: Soybean is a major oilseed and protein crop that improves soil fertility through nitrogen fixation.
soybean.common_uses: Edible oil extraction, high-protein soy meal for poultry/livestock, and food products.
soybean.soil: Well-drained fertile black cotton soils or deep loams.
soybean.climate: Warm and moist climate with temperature around 26°C–32°C.
soybean.key_characteristics: Leguminous crop that fixes atmospheric nitrogen; enriches soil for next crop.

cotton.why_grown: Cotton (White Gold) is India's primary commercial fibre crop, supporting the textile industry.
cotton.common_uses: Textile fibre, surgical cotton, cottonseed oil, and oilcake feed.
cotton.soil: Deep black cotton soils (Vertisols) or fertile alluvial soils.
cotton.climate: Uniformly high temperature (21°C–30°C) with clear sunny days during boll formation.
cotton.key_characteristics: Long duration cash crop; benefits from integrated pest management.

sugarcane.why_grown: Sugarcane is a long-duration industrial commercial crop powering the sugar and ethanol sector.
sugarcane.common_uses: Sugar, jaggery (gur), molasses, ethanol biofuel, and bagasse for paper/energy.
sugarcane.soil: Deep, well-drained loams or clay loams with neutral pH.
sugarcane.climate: Tropical and subtropical climate with long sunny periods and ample moisture.
sugarcane.key_characteristics: High water and nutrient requirements; excellent ratoon cropping capability.

chickpea (gram).why_grown: Chickpea (Chana) is India's top Rabi pulse crop, crucial for soil health and pulse production.
chickpea (gram).common_uses: Whole pulse (chana), dal, besan (gram flour), and roasted snacks.
chickpea (gram).soil: Well-drained medium-to-heavy loams or sandy loams.
chickpea (gram).climate: Cool and dry weather; highly sensitive to high humidity and rain at flowering.
chickpea (gram).key_characteristics: Improves soil nitrogen balance; low water requirement.

moong (green gram).why_grown: Moong is a short-duration pulse crop ideal for crop rotation and quick farm income.
moong (green gram).common_uses: Dal, sprouts, soups, and green manure.
moong (green gram).season: Kharif, Summer (Zaid), and Rabi in south India.
moong (green gram).soil: Well-drained loamy or sandy loam soils.
moong (green gram).climate: Warm climate (25°C–35°C); tolerant to brief high temperatures.
moong (green gram).key_characteristics: Short duration (60–75 days); fixes nitrogen and restores soil health.

black gram (urad).why_grown: Urad is a high-protein legume crop cultivated widely in Kharif and Summer seasons.
black gram (urad).common_uses: Dal, fermented batters (idli/dosa), and green fodder.
black gram (urad).soil: Well-drained fertile loams or black soils.
black gram (urad).climate: Hot and humid climate during vegetative growth.
black gram (urad).key_characteristics: Fixes atmospheric nitrogen; prevents soil erosion due to canopy cover.

pigeonpea (arhar/tur).why_grown: Pigeonpea (Tur) is a major deep-rooted Kharif pulse providing high dietary protein.
pigeonpea (arhar/tur).common_uses: Tur dal (yellow split pulse) and green vegetable pods.
pigeonpea (arhar/tur).soil: Deep, well-drained loams or medium clay soils.
pigeonpea (arhar/tur).climate: Warm tropical climate with moderate seasonal rainfall.
pigeonpea (arhar/tur).key_characteristics: Deep taproot system opens subsoil; highly drought tolerant.

groundnut.why_grown: Groundnut (Peanut) is an important oilseed and food legume crop in rainfed regions.
groundnut.common_uses: Edible oil, roasted peanut snacks, peanut butter, and oilcake fodder.
groundnut.soil: Well-drained sandy loam or light sandy soil for easy peg penetration.
groundnut.climate: Warm climate with 22°C–30°C temperature and sunny weather.
groundnut.key_characteristics: Requires light soil texture for pod development; fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

banana.why_grown: Banana is a high-value commercial fruit crop offering year-round harvesting and income.
banana.common_uses: Fresh fruit consumption, banana chips, fibre, and traditional leaves for serving.
banana.soil: Rich, deep, well-drained loamy soil with high organic matter.
banana.climate: Warm, humid tropical climate with uniform moisture.
banana.key_characteristics: Heavy feeder of nutrients and water; continuous yield cycle.

coconut.why_grown: Coconut (Kalpavriksha) is a premier perennial palm crop supporting coastal farming livelihoods.
coconut.common_uses: Fresh tender water, copra, coconut oil, coir fibre, and culinary use.
coconut.soil: Coastal alluvial, sandy loam, or lateritic soils.
coconut.climate: Warm humid tropical climate with well-distributed rainfall.
coconut.key_characteristics: Perennial crop yielding for 60+ years; intercropping compatible.

arecanut.why_grown: Arecanut (Betelnut) is a high-value plantation crop cultivated in humid tropical zones.
arecanut.common_uses: Masticatory use, industrial tannins, and processing products.
arecanut.soil: Deep, well-drained red clay loams or laterite soils.
arecanut.climate: Humid tropical climate with high humidity and abundant rainfall.
arecanut.key_characteristics: Requires shade in early growth; highly profitable long-term crop.

horse-gram.why_grown: Horse-gram (Kulthi) is a hardy drought-resistant pulse crop grown in marginal soils.
horse-gram.common_uses: Nutritious pulse, traditional medicinal preparations, and animal feed.
horse-gram.soil: Poor, shallow, sandy or gravelly soils where other crops struggle.
horse-gram.climate: Dry, warm climate; exceptional drought endurance.
horse-gram.key_characteristics: Requires minimal inputs; excellent green manure and ground cover.

sorghum.why_grown: Sorghum (Jowar) is a resilient nutrient-dense coarse cereal ideal for dryland agriculture.
sorghum.common_uses: Roti (flatbread), poultry feed, sweet sorghum ethanol, and dry fodder.
sorghum.soil: Medium to deep black clay soils or fertile loams.
sorghum.climate: Warm dry climate; high temperature and drought resistance.
sorghum.key_characteristics: Extremely water efficient; dual-purpose crop for grain and fodder.

pearl millet (bajra).why_grown: Bajra is a hardy nutri-cereal cultivated in arid and semi-arid regions.
pearl millet (bajra).common_uses: Traditional flatbreads, porridge, cattle fodder, and bio-fortified foods.
pearl millet (bajra).soil: Light sandy loams or well-drained shallow soils.
pearl millet (bajra).climate: Hot, dry climate with low rainfall capability.
pearl millet (bajra).key_characteristics: High heat and drought tolerance; rich in iron and zinc.

finger millet (ragi).why_grown: Ragi is a superfood nutri-cereal rich in calcium, iron, and dietary fibre.
finger millet (ragi).common_uses: Ragi malt, porridge, mudde, bakery items, and infant food.
finger millet (ragi).season: Kharif and Rabi in south India.
finger millet (ragi).soil: Red loam, sandy loam, or clay loam soils.
finger millet (ragi).climate: Adaptable climate; grows well in moderate rainfall belts.
finger millet (ragi).key_characteristics: Excellent grain storage life; resistant to major grain pests.
